description: conformance-history-graph-tree.json resolved on one tile. The chart geometry is the point: a renderer that plots the series correctly but anchors the band, the area or the end points differently draws a visibly different graph from the same tree.

conformance.note: a layer gives every child the whole content box, in declaration order, first one furthest back

conformance.dense.area: the line, closed down to y=240 at both ends - the fill reaches the element's bottom edge, not the band's top

conformance.sparse.note: a stack justified to the end, so its one child sits against the foot of the box

conformance.sparse.chart.bandNote: no plotTop, so the band is the whole element

conformance.empty.draws: nothing at all - neither line nor fill. A flat line along the foot of the band would read as a real value of zero.

conformance.content.title.note: 26.4 from the basis, held to 12.996 by the cell - this is the clamp that keeps a nine-cell card from reading as a poster

conformance.content.subtitle.note: the cell clamp is present but far above the basis term, so it does not bind - a renderer that ignored maxOfCell would pass on this run alone

conformance.value.note: no padding, justified and aligned centre, so the row's centre is the card's centre

conformance.value.row.alignNote: the two runs' text sits on one line; their boxes do not line up, and must not be made to

conformance.value.row.reading.minWidth: 3.5 digit advances of the face it is drawn in, the content centred within it when narrower
